name: 45Q credit claimants

summary.text: Section 45Q of the Internal Revenue Code gives a tax credit for carbon oxide that is captured and either stored geologically or used, including in enhanced oil recovery. The Treasury Inspector General for Tax Administration (TIGTA) analysed credits claimed for tax years 2010 to 2019 at the request of Senator Robert Menendez and reported in April 2020 that ten taxpayers accounted for almost all of the roughly $1 billion claimed, and that about $894 million of it had been claimed while the claimants did not have an EPA-approved monitoring, reporting and verification plan. The IRS and Treasury issued final 45Q regulations in January 2021.

sources.title: TIGTA Says Numerous Improper Carbon Oxide Credits Claimed

facts.claim: On April 15, 2020 TIGTA answered a November 2019 request from Senator Robert Menendez about gaps between section 45Q credits claimed and the sequestered carbon reported to EPA, analysing credits claimed for tax years 2010 through 2019.

sources.title: TIGTA Says Numerous Improper Carbon Oxide Credits Claimed
IRC 45Q Credit Under IRS Scrutiny: Government Finds Majority of Carbon Oxide Credits Improperly Claimed

facts.claim: TIGTA found that of 672 taxpayers reporting carbon dioxide sequestration to the IRS, ten claimed more than $1 million each, and those ten accounted for over $1 billion, about 99.9 percent, of all 45Q credits claimed.
facts.quote: 10 taxpayers (one and a half percent) claimed over $1 million each, with their claims totaling over $1 billion (99.9 percent) of all of the I.R.C. 45Q credits

sources.title: TIGTA Says Numerous Improper Carbon Oxide Credits Claimed
IRS Implementation of the Carbon Oxide Sequestration Credit (45Q)

facts.claim: TIGTA reported that $893,935,025, or 87 percent of the credits, had been claimed by those ten taxpayers when they did not have an approved EPA monitoring, reporting and verification (MRV) plan in place at the time the credit was claimed; only three of the ten had an approved plan at the time of the analysis.
facts.quote: $893,935,025 (87 percent) worth of 45Q credits were claimed by these 10 taxpayers when they were not in compliance with the EPA, i.e., they did not have an approved MRV Plan in place at the time the credit was claimed

sources.title: TIGTA Says Numerous Improper Carbon Oxide Credits Claimed
Treasury IG: A decade of carbon-capture tax credits were faulty

facts.claim: TIGTA reported that the IRS had already taken action against four of the ten large claimants, disallowing roughly 60 percent of the credits that had been claimed without an approved EPA plan.

sources.title: IRC 45Q Credit Under IRS Scrutiny: Government Finds Majority of Carbon Oxide Credits Improperly Claimed
IRC 45Q Credit Under IRS Scrutiny: Government Finds Majority of Carbon Oxide Credits Improperly Claimed

facts.claim: On April 29, 2020 Senator Menendez wrote to IRS Commissioner Charles Rettig attaching TIGTA's analysis and asking the IRS, among other things, to suspend the 45Q credit for enhanced oil recovery pending a full investigation.

sources.title: Menendez Calls on IRS to Enforce Carbon Oxide Credit Compliance
Menendez presses IRS on fossil fuel tax credits after inspector general report

facts.claim: The Treasury Department and IRS published final regulations on the credit for carbon oxide sequestration (TD 9944) in the Federal Register on January 15, 2021.

sources.title: TD 9944, Credit for Carbon Oxide Sequestration

facts.claim: A September 2024 report by Taxpayers for Common Sense on IRS implementation of the 45Q credit said no further public updates on the compliance problems identified by TIGTA had been provided since April 2020.

sources.title: IRS Implementation of the Carbon Oxide Sequestration Credit (45Q)

connections.claim: Claimants of the 45Q credit are required to have an EPA-approved monitoring, reporting and verification plan for the sequestered carbon; TIGTA found that 87 percent of the credits claimed by the ten largest claimants had been claimed without such an approved plan in place.
connections.quote: they did not have an approved MRV Plan in place at the time the credit was claimed

openQuestions: Site claim 'about $894 million of roughly $1 billion in 45Q credits went to companies that had not met EPA monitoring requirements' is supported: TIGTA's figure is $893,935,025 (87 percent) of just over $1 billion claimed by ten taxpayers.

Site claim 'Much captured CO2 was used to pump more oil' is consistent with Senator Menendez's April 2020 request that the credit for enhanced oil recovery be suspended, but TIGTA's letter as summarised does not quantify how much captured CO2 went to enhanced oil recovery; the owner may want a source for the share.

The TIGTA letter itself was not located on tigta.gov; the record above rests on the Tax Notes reproduction of the letter and on law-firm and press summaries. The owner may wish to find the original on tigta.gov.
TIGTA did not name the ten taxpayers; no source identifies the claimants, so this entry cannot be linked to specific companies.
